messages:
jamal: noticing a sharp increase in gRPC stream stalls between pods in us-west-2 GPU pool after last night's node upgrade. Pods hang during long-lived responses (streaming logits).

maria: saw it too, alerts spiked ~00:12. Any packet drops on host?

jamal: running quick check, looks like some nodes have differing NIC MTUs on the egress path. suspecting PMTU issues with encapsulation (vxlan + ipip).

kai: can you paste ip link / route outputs?

jamal: sure, from node gpu-12: ```
$ ip link show eno1
3: eno1: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
$ ip link show vxlan0
43: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default
```

jamal: but on node gpu-07 the vxlan mtu is 1500 while underlying eno1 is 1500 too. inconsistent encap overheads.

ben: that's weird — we expected all vxlan interfaces to be 1450 after the new CNI release. rollout might have been partial.

infra-bot: incident 2026-03-20-01 created: "pod->pod gRPC stall - probable MTU mismatch" assigned to @jamal, @maria

maria: tcpdump on the pod-to-pod path shows ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages being blocked or ignored (DF set). snippet: ```
13:04:12.345678 IP 10.2.1.45 > 10.2.3.12: IP, id 0, frag 0, proto TCP, length 1480
13:04:12.345679 IP 10.2.3.12 > 10.2.1.45: ICMP frag needed and DF set (mtu 1450)
```

maria: but we don't see the ICMP reaching the sender on some node pairs. feels like an offload or DPU path dropping those messages.

kai: any SR-IOV or DPU offload changes in the upgrade? I remember we toggled GSO/GRO offload on a subset of nodes as an experiment.

jamal: yes, last night some racks were auto-upgraded and the cloud image now has dpdk driver + VF offload enabled by default on select SKUs.

ben: that matches — if offloaded frames bypass kernel PMTU handling the DF/ICMP flow might be suppressed (blackhole). gRPC streams with large frames will stall because TCP never learns smaller MTU.

maria: reproducer: from pod A -> pod B run a long streaming request and `ss -tin` shows send window not advancing, retransmits, then stall.

jamal: quick mitigation: force the node-level MTU to the lowest common denominator and clamp vxlan to 1400 on all nodes, or disable offload on the DPU path. patch rolling now to 10 nodes.

kai: preference is clamp + config rollback in CNI so it's consistent across fleet. disabling offload is higher risk for throughput on GPU workloads.

ben: agree — do both: immediate clamp on all active nodes for stability, and schedule a controlled canary for the offload setting toggles. will open a dedicated change with rollback steps.

infra-bot: change request CR-4821 opened: "enforce vxlan mtu 1400 on gpu pools + canary offload toggle" assigned to @ben

sre-oncall: tracking customer-facing impact? any retries at API layer? we should enable automatic fallback to smaller chunking sizes for streaming endpoints in the API gateway.

maria: good call — will add a temporary middleware to chunk stream frames to <1400 until fleet is consistent. small perf hit but better than timeouts.

jamal: rolling clamp to 1400 on us-west-2 first 20 nodes now. posting results in ~10m.

(10 minutes later)

jamal: update: after clamps, gRPC stalls on affected pods cleared. metrics show streaming latency returned to baseline.

kai: next steps: 1) run fleet-wide audit for any nodes with offload/drivers mismatch 2) add unit in upgrade pipeline that validates vxlan/overlay mtu equals underlying path mtu minus encaps overhead 3) add probe that verifies ICMP frag-needed path is not blackholed before marking node healthy.

ben: I'll schedule the canary for offload toggles and draft runbook for future kernel/CNI upgrades.

maria: creating a short postmortem and linking CR/PRs. also adding a k8s admission check to prevent mixed CNI configs in the same nodepool.

sre-oncall: thanks team — keeping this thread for the postmortem notes and runbook. :thumbsup:
